title: RDW-to-albumin ratio did not improve cross-cohort CRP prediction beyond flexible component measures
abstract: The red-cell distribution-width-to-albumin ratio (RAR) is an established prognostic composite. We asked whether its raw ratio representation adds nonadditive information about concurrent log C-reactive protein beyond flexible component and standard physiological measures. Models trained in 4063 NHANES2005–2006 adults were frozen and evaluated in 5147 different NHANES2007–2008 adults. MEC-weighted MSE was 1.063148 without and 1.063218 with RAR; gain was -0.000069 (500 source-refit/target-resample rescaled PSU bootstrap95% interval -0.003517 to 0.000938). No incremental prediction benefit was demonstrated. Small benefits or harms remain compatible. This representation-specific negative result does not test mortality, causality or clinical utility. Validation uses separate recruitment cohorts within one survey platform, not independent health systems.
